definition: Every assembly on the plate rises up the wall plane, bottom to top, as a wall section does. A casing is really measured across its face, from the jamb outward, so its widths appear here as heights; the plate does not turn it.
basis: Our wording, read from the pack schema's assemblies field and the classical trim family's casing member notes. schema/proportion-pack.schema.json, assemblies description: "Each assembly is a stack of members, bottom to top, dimensioned in PARTS of the module."; proportions/systems/trim-classical.json assemblies.casing_georgian.members[geo_cas_reveal].note: "This assembly is measured ACROSS the casing from the jamb outward rather than vertically; height_parts is therefore a width."; proportions/systems/trim-classical.json assemblies.casing_federal.members[fed_cas_reveal].note: "Measured across the casing, as in the Georgian assembly.".
